title: License one market-price source, even a small one
what_would_change: Fills market_line_* and difference_* on every originated row, unblocks D966-STR-09, and makes closing-line value and edge decay real measurements instead of blanks. Roughly half the requirement list is written against a number this pack cannot see.
why_now: The store, the columns and the gate are already built around the absence, so adding a price later is an ingest, not a rewrite.
cost_or_effort: one source decision plus one ingest module; the ledger and the difference columns already exist
risk_if_applied: operator pages carry redistribution terms of their own; a licensed feed removes that question, a scraped one creates it
risk_if_not_applied: edge, CLV and the ROI claim stay unavailable forever, and the leaderboard keeps ranking against our own prices
applied_by_default: no - the human picks the path before anything changes
evidence_or_source: four capture attempts recorded in price_capture_attempts.csv

title: Backfill Weeks 1-6 into the results feed
what_would_change: Takes the graded window from 44 games to about 136, which lifts the moneyline gap (flag D966-F10) away, narrows every correlation interval, and lets dispersion and the damping factor be fitted before Week 7 instead of on the window they are used in.
why_now: the ingest is one page per week at the URL pattern already in capture.py; the identity checks and the reconciliation were written to scale to it unchanged
cost_or_effort: six page reads and six table appends; no new code
risk_if_applied: more rows to keep honest; a mid-season rule change or roster turnover can make early-week rates a worse prior than late-week ones
risk_if_not_applied: every coefficient published today sits under flag D966-F08 for small n
applied_by_default: no - the human picks the path before anything changes
evidence_or_source: correlations.csv n column; results_feed.csv week coverage

title: Write the settlement conventions down as a file the site displays
what_would_change: Push, tie, no-contest and void handling are declared in backtest.py's docstring today. A published rules file means a graded result can be re-derived by someone else without reading Python.
why_now: the tie probability is now non-zero (0.0273 on the Washington-Giants line), so push handling changes numbers rather than being a footnote
cost_or_effort: one short document, generated from the same constants the code uses
risk_if_applied: the file must then be kept in sync with the code, which is a real cost over a year
risk_if_not_applied: a settlement disagreement later becomes an argument about what we meant
applied_by_default: no - the human picks the path before anything changes
evidence_or_source: backtest.py module docstring; originated_lines.csv tie probability column

title: Ingest official per-player game statistics so prop combos can settle
what_would_change: Unblocks D966-STR-10 and correlation candidate D966-CX-02: a prop leg could be settled from a box score, and a prop-team parlay could be priced with a measured dependence instead of an assumption.
why_now: the parlay machinery (legs, push handling, joint probability from a measured rho) is already written; only the axis is missing
cost_or_effort: a box-score ingest per game plus a player-id join against the injury report
risk_if_applied: player-name joins are where misattribution happens; a wrong join settles a leg wrong, so the id join needs its own identity check
risk_if_not_applied: prop combinations stay specified-but-ungraded, which is the weakest place in the brief's list
applied_by_default: no - the human picks the path before anything changes

title: Add an official playing-time source so depth can be weighted, not counted
what_would_change: Tiers-dropped is a lower bound built from designations. Snap counts or a published depth chart would let the deficit be weighted by how much a club actually plays the position.
why_now: the column already carries a score_kind that says the weighting is a proposal; a real weight would replace the proposal rather than add to it
cost_or_effort: a source with redistribution rights; none of the pages read for this pack qualify
risk_if_applied: third-party depth charts are estimates with their own model error - swapping one guess for a better-documented one is still a guess unless it is labelled
risk_if_not_applied: depth keeps reporting a floor, and the club rollup keeps understating
applied_by_default: no - the human picks the path before anything changes

title: Decide whether cross-version movement belongs in the open/close column
what_would_change: 26 markets currently show movement between the prior session's model and ours. Either keep the number with flag D966-F02 attached (today's choice) or blank it and move the figure to a separate model_revision_delta column.
why_now: the column exists and is being read; a decision now prevents it being quoted as market movement later
cost_or_effort: one column and one sentence in the builder
risk_if_applied: blanking it hides the only measured movement available, which readers may want
risk_if_not_applied: a model rewrite gets quoted as if the market moved

risk_if_applied: if the two reads disagree, we then hold two versions of the same report and must say which one every table used
risk_if_not_applied: depth counts for six clubs keep an unexplained attribution
applied_by_default: no - the human picks the path before anything changes

title: Let the demotion gate run before publication, not after
what_would_change: The gate is computed in the same run today, after the tables are written. Running it first would let the site refuse to publish a strategy that fails, instead of publishing it and labelling it paper.
why_now: one strategy was promoted and nine held back on real numbers; the ordering question starts to matter the moment the pack runs daily
cost_or_effort: reorder the builder; keep the failing rows published either way
risk_if_applied: refusing to publish is worse for review than publishing with a reason - the failing row would become invisible, which is what flags exist to prevent
risk_if_not_applied: a strategy can appear on the board for one run before it is sent back
applied_by_default: no - the human picks the path before anything changes

title: Decide whether rewards stay non-monetary
what_would_change: The tier table pays in standing, compute priority and a badge. Cash would change the incentive from 'be accurate' to 'be profitable', and it runs into the rights position the prior session recorded for league data.
why_now: the reward table is written; changing its currency later changes what strategies optimise for
risk_if_applied: monetary reward on betting outcomes in a project built on league data invites both the rights question and a regulatory one
risk_if_not_applied: none material - standing is what an autonomous leaderboard can grant itself
applied_by_default: no - the human picks the path before anything changes
